_source: Letsios, Kouyialis, Misener (2018), Heuristics with performance guarantees for the minimum number of matches problem in heat recovery network design, Computers and Chemical Engineering 113, 57-85. Values from data/tex_tables/exact_methods.tex of github.com/TYT0710/min_matches_heuristics (commit 60894d2), column 'Gurobi Transshipment' (all four solver columns agree for these instances).
_solver_gap: Solved with relative gap 4 % (table caption). A value v reported without a remaining gap is therefore proven optimal when 0.04 v < 1, i.e. v <= 24; above that it is within 4 % of the optimum.
_instances: Furman and Sahinidis (2004) test set, digitised by Letsios et al. (Apache License 2.0, see LICENSE-Apache-2.0 and references.txt). Line endings converted from CRLF to LF; content unchanged.

_excluded.22sp-ph: infeasible here: HS9 is cooled to 8 °C but the only cold utility enters at 20 °C, so at ΔTmin 10 K that heat has nowhere to go under the shifted-temperature convention; the original code must treat the instance differently (not investigated)
_excluded.14sp1: published 14 (proven, CPLEX 41 s); HiGHS reaches 14 but does not prove it within 60 s, too slow for the regeneration run
_excluded.37sp-yfyv: published 36 (within 4 %); HiGHS stops at 37 after 60 s
